'''Emilia Kilpua''' (born November 18, 1977, in [[Oulu]]) is a Finnish [[Outline of space science|space scientist]]. She is currently Professor of Space Physics at the [[University of Helsinki]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emilia Kilpua |url=https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/persons/emilia-kilpua |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=University of Helsinki |language=en}}</ref>

== Background and career ==
Kilpua was born and raised in Oulu, northern Finland, where [[aurora|auroras]] are commonplace in winter. She studied theoretical physics and mathematics at the [[University of Helsinki]], followed by a [[Master's degree]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]], with a thesis titled [[Shock waves in astrophysics|''Interplanetary shocks'']]'', [[Coronal mass ejection|magnetic clouds]] and [[Geomagnetic storm|magnetospheric storms]]'', which she completed in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Emilia Kilpua |url=https://multiverse.ssl.berkeley.edu/Solar-Week/Meet-the-Scientists/Emilia-Kilpua |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=multiverse.ssl.berkeley.edu}}</ref> She undertook a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research associate]] post in the [[Space Sciences Laboratory]] at [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]] for three years. She moved back to Finland in 2008.

== Scientific interests ==
Kilpua's primary research focus is [[space weather]], particularly with an eye to improving forecasting.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tiedeykkönen: Aurinko on monimutkainen hiukkaskattila - Venus ja Jupiter loistavat tähtitaivaalla {{!}} Yle Areena – podcastit |url=https://areena.yle.fi/audio/1-3880772 |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=areena.yle.fi |language=fi}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Keränen |first=Matti |title=Vuonna 2012 Aurinko oli lähellä täräyttää kunnolla maapalloa - Avaruustutkija Emilia Kilpua hyötyi hurjasti: "Se osoittautui yhdeksi mittaushistorian voimakkaimmista magneettikentistä" |url=https://www.tekniikkatalous.fi/uutiset/vuonna-2012-aurinko-oli-lahella-tarayttaa-kunnolla-maapalloa-avaruustutkija-emilia-kilpua-hyotyi-hurjasti-se-osoittautui-yhdeksi-mittaushistorian-voimakkaimmista-magneettikentista/8f07fe59-fba6-3316-8a92-ad1f40232ed4 |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=Tekniikka&Talous |date=10 February 2018 |language=fi}}</ref> She has made advances in our understanding of the formation and propagation of [[coronal mass ejection]]s to Earth,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-11 |title=Euroopan aurinkoluotain kuvaa Auringon navat |url=https://www.tiede.fi/artikkeli/uutiset/euroopan-aurinkoluotain-kuvaa-auringon-navat |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=Tiede |language=fi}}</ref> as well as the response of the magnetospheric system, particularly the Earth's [[Van Allen radiation belt|radiation belts]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-82167-8 |title=Physics of Earth's Radiation Belts |series=Astronomy and Astrophysics Library |year=2022 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-82167-8|isbn=978-3-030-82166-1 |s2cid=240322137 |last1=Koskinen |first1=Hannu E. J. |last2=Kilpua |first2=Emilia K. J. }}</ref> Since 2021, she has been a coordinator of the H2020 Marie Skłodowska-Curie Innovative Training Network SWATNet to train early career scientists in the field of heliosphysics and space weather. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Emilia Kilpua - Biography |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Kilpua_Emilia/CV |website=Academy of Europe}}</ref>

*2021: [[Väisälä Prize]] of the [[Finnish Academy of Science and Letters|Finnish Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tiedeakatemia myönsi Väisälä-palkinnot professori Emilia Kilpualle ja apulaisprofessori Christian Webbille {{!}} Helsingin yliopisto |url=https://www.helsinki.fi/fi/uutiset/avaruus/tiedeakatemia-myonsi-vaisala-palkinnot-professori-emilia-kilpualle-ja-apulaisprofessori-christian-webbille |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=www.helsinki.fi |date=13 December 2021 |language=fi}}</ref>

*2017: 2021 Member of Board of Solar Physics Division - European Physical Society
